 Crl.Rev.Pet.No.1933 Of 2011

 Order

Dated this the 30th day of July 2020 The petitioners are the accused 1 to 3 respectively in S.T.No.1132/2007 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kunnamangalam and the appellant in Crl.Appeal No.614/2009 on the filed of the Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track (Adhoc-II), Kozhikode.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kunnamangalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. By judgment dated 19.09.2009, the learned Magistrate convicted and sentenced accused 1 to 3 to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year each and also to pay a fine of Rs.1000/- each,
in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for one month more for the offence punishable under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 7(i), 2(1)(a)(m) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
Challenging the conviction and sentence, accused 1 to 3 preferred Criminal Appeal No.614/2009 before the Session Court, Kozhikode.
The learned Session Judge made over the case to the Additional Sessions Court for hearing.
The learned Additional Sessions Judge dismissed the appeal by judgment dated 07.07.2011 confirming the conviction and sentence Crl.Rev.Pet.No.1933 OF 2011 imposed by the learned Magistrate.
Being aggrieved, the accused 1 to 3 preferred this revision.

3. The prosecution cases in brief, is that on 29.03.2007, the Food Inspector, Kunnamangalam Circle inspected a milk- sales van bearing No.KL-07-8471 on 29.03.2007 and purchased three packets of pasteurized tonned milk containing 500ml each from the stock of 15 packets kept inside the plastic tray on payment of Rs.22.50/-
After complying with all legal formalities for sampling, one sample was sent to the public analyst for report.
The public analyst submitted his report stating that upon analysis of the sample of milk, the sample does not conform the prescribed standard for tonned milk.
The said sample was therefore adulterated within the meaning of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the Rules framed thereunder.
4. Based upon the report of the public analyst, the learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence and issued process against accused 1 to 3.

The public analyst by Form III report opined that the sample is not conforming to the standard prescribed for tonned milk and as per Ext.P13, milk fat was noted as 2.9, and as per the standard, it shall not be less than Crl.Rev.Pet.No.1933 OF 2011 3%,
and Solids Not Fat (SNF) was noted as 7.6% and as per the standard, it shall not be less than 8.5%.
5. Being aggrieved by the finding in Ext.P13, another part of the sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory under Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act and Ext.P26 Form II certificate was obtained.

Ext.P26 Form II certificate would show that the milk fat as 7.6% (as per standard it shall not be less than 3%) and Solid Not Fat (SNF) noted as 5.15% (as per the Act not less than 8.5%).

2

6. Heard Sri.Santhosh Subramanian, the learned counsel for the revision petitioners and Sri.M.S.Breeze, the learned Public Prosecutor.
7.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioners filed this criminal revision petition before this court as early as on 09.08.2011.

One of the main grounds taken by the learned counsel for the revision petitioners in the revision petition is narrated as herein below:
"F) Mandatory provisions of law contained in Sections 23(1) (A) (ee) (hh) of the Act are violated in this case and the Laboratories in which Ext.P13 was issued was not a defined laboratory and those rules relating to the establishment of the laboratory were not laid before Crl.Rev.Pet.No.1933 OF 2011 parliament as required in Section 23(2) of the P.F.A. Act and Ext.P26 certificate was issued by the Laboratory and those labs are not defined laboratory and the methods followed are not laid before parliament and not published and defined and the general public and industry are not informed nor those methods are appended in the Act or Rule nor published in official gazettes and as such are secret method which are illegal and hence no legal sanctity can be given to Ext.P13 and P26 and they are liable to be rejected and dismissed by this Hon'ble Court and as prescribed in Rule 3(c) of the PFA Rules standarised methods of analysis are to be followed in all laboratories and the lack of defined laboratories as per law and lack of standarised methods of analysis and as laid before parliament and published and appended in the Rules and in the absence of such mandatory requirements of law the entire procedure were vitiated and Courts below had not considered those aspects."
8.

In Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and Another [2010 (4) KHC 767], the apex court held that in order to form a foundation for the prosecution after 01.04.1976, ie., the date of incorporation of the provisions under Section 23(1A) (ee), the report of the public analyst must be one based on the analysis from a laboratory defined under Section 23(1A) (ee) following the procedure provided under Section 23(1A) (hh).

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and Another [2010 (4) KHC 767]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ext.P13 Form III report in the instant case cannot be said to be made based on an analysis conducted in such a Crl.Rev.Pet.No.1933 OF 2011 laboratory.
In the said circumstances, this Court is of the view that cognizance could not have been taken on the complaint based on Ext.P12.

On the date of presentation of the complaint, the learned Magistrate was legally prohibited from by taking cognizance of the offences enumerated in the complaint in the absence of a valid Form III report as per the scheme of the Act.
In the above circumstances, no useful purpose could have been served by sending the second sample to the Central Forensic Laboratory.
Form II report submitted by the Central Food Laboratory is insignificant for the just decision of this case.

The decision of the apex court in Pepsico India Holdings's case is followed by a Division Bench of this Court in Raheed N.K. v. Food Inspector, Thalassery and Another [2016 (2)
KHC 679].

entities.text:
Raheed N.K. v. Food Inspector, Thalassery and Another [2016 (2)
KHC 679]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The apex court as well as this Court consistently held that till the repealing of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, no laboratories from where a Public Analyst to conduct an analysis in terms of Section 23(1A) (ee) were defined.
Hence, there could not have been a report after conducting a analysis in such a laboratory defined in terms of the aforesaid provisions.

sentences.text: In the result, this revision petition is allowed.
The Crl.Rev.Pet.No.1933 OF 2011 conviction and sentence imposed against the revision petitioners/accused stand set aside.

The revision petitioners/accused 1 to 3 are found not guilty for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i)
read with Section 7(i), 2(1)
(a)(m) of the P.F.A Act and they are acquitted for the said offences thereunder.
Cancelling their bail bonds, this court directs that they be set at liberty.
Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.

Sd/-
